subject: Latest ez might (appear to) break old code

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Latest ez might (appear to) break old code
parts:
Hi folks,

I meant to send this note out earlier but failed for no good reason. 

You might have noticed that the latest version of ez (4.2-2) leaves you with code that no longer works. The big change with 4.2-2 is that ez no longer automatically loads the various packages on which it relies internally. It *does* still use those packages in the background, but the functions in the packages are not available to you as the user until you explicitly load them yourself. 

So, if you have code that, for example, used the ddply() function from the plyr package, you previously could simply load ez via library(ez) and ddply() would be ready for use, but now you have to explicitly load plyr via library(plyr). Ditto ggplot2, stringr, lme4, etc.

To reiterate, if you were starting with a fresh R instance, the following previously worked:

    library(ez)
    ddply

But this now should fail, throwing an error that ddply could not be found. What you have to do now is:

    library(ez)
    library(plyr)
    ddply



Mike
